description: Matthew Kuhn's unofficial ascelike class v3.0 (2025/03/17, CTAN and MiKTeX package ascelike, LPPL 1.1 or later), the ASCE journal and proceedings manuscript format; ASCE's official Overleaf template uses ascelike-new.cls, derived from it and not in MiKTeX. Journal is the class default and the mode of ASCE's official template: article at 12pt, one column, letter paper, double spaced (setspace) with line numbers (lineno), both loaded at \begin{document}. The bundle's example uses Proceedings instead (single spaced, no line numbers). The class loads babel (american), newtxtext, newtxmath, microtype and authblk itself; under XeTeX newtxtext sets TeX Gyre Termes X through fontspec. It needed nothing in the preamble for its own sake: without biblatex it keeps its own BibTeX \cite code for ascelike.bst and only writes a note to the log (ascelike.cls l.777-781); with biblatex it passes style=ascelike and backend=biber (l.652). General's lmodern, fontspec, Latin Modern main and sans fonts and amssymb are left out (omitPreamble): the class's newtxtext and newtxmath set the fonts, and amssymb stops at "\Bbbk already defined". \let\openbox\undefined lets General's amsthm define \openbox, which newtxmath already did (batch 2 probe). At \begin{document}, if paralist or enumerate is loaded, their enumerate (and paralist's itemize) end as plain lists: the class's list code closed them with \end{list}, and documents stopped at "\begin{enumerate} ... ended by \end{list}" (round b27: 172 of 174 error cells; fix session's probe: 6 and 30 errors before, 0 after).
